documents.note: Source: The Highway Code, Annex 3 (Motor vehicle documentation and learner driver requirements).

items.text: Cars and motorcycles MUST normally pass an MOT test three years from the date of the first registration and every year after that.
You MUST have a valid insurance certificate covering you for third-party liability before using a motor vehicle on the road.
Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) MUST be paid on all motor vehicles used or kept on public roads. A Statutory Off Road Notification (SORN) must be made if the vehicle is unused and untaxed.
If the police ask to see your driving licence, insurance certificate or MOT certificate and you cannot do so, you may be asked to take them to a police station within 7 days.
Any vehicle driven by a learner MUST display red L plates which conform to legal specifications. Plates should be removed or covered when not being driven by a learner.
Learner drivers in a car MUST be supervised by someone at least 21 years old who holds a full EC/EEA licence for that type of car and has held it for at least three years.
Under the New Drivers Act, a driver who accumulates six or more penalty points within two years of passing their first driving test will have their licence revoked.

vehicleMaintenance.note: Source: The Highway Code, Annex 6 (Vehicle maintenance, safety and security).
vehicleMaintenance.tyres: Cars, light vans and light trailers MUST have a tread depth of at least 1.6 mm across the central three-quarters of the breadth of the tyre and around the entire circumference. Motorcycles, large vehicles and passenger-carrying vehicles MUST have a tread depth of at least 1 mm.
vehicleMaintenance.fluids: Check fluid levels (oil, coolant, brake fluid, screenwash) regularly. Top up screenwash to keep the windscreen clean — it is an offence to have an empty screenwash bottle if the system is fitted.
vehicleMaintenance.lights: Check that all lights, indicators, reflectors and number plate lights work and are clean.
vehicleMaintenance.battery: Check the battery, particularly in winter. Modern maintenance-free batteries should not need topping up.
vehicleMaintenance.exhaust: Excessive exhaust fumes could indicate a fault — have the vehicle checked. You MUST NOT drive a vehicle with a defective exhaust system.

firstAid.note: Source: The Highway Code, Annex 7 (First aid on the road).
firstAid.drabc: D — Danger: check it is safe to approach. R — Response: try to get a response by gently shaking shoulders. A — Airway: tilt the head back gently. B — Breathing: look, listen and feel for normal breathing for up to 10 seconds. C — Circulation/CPR: if not breathing normally, start CPR (30 chest compressions then 2 rescue breaths).
firstAid.burns: Cool the burn for at least 20 minutes with cool water. Do not remove anything sticking to the burn.
firstAid.shock: Keep casualties warm and as comfortable as you can; reassure them; do not give them anything to eat or drink.
